question: A 36-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after the onset of progressively worsening upper abdominal pain and 4 episodes of vomiting. His father had a myocardial infarction at the age of 40 years. Physical examination shows tenderness and guarding in the epigastrium. Bowel sounds are decreased. His serum amylase is 400 U/L. Symptomatic treatment and therapy with fenofibrate are initiated. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opd: Separate dorsal and ventral pancreatic ducts

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with upper abdominal pain" -> "Serum amylase is elevated" -> "Suggestive of pancreatitis" -> "Fenofibrate is initiated" -> "Fenofibrate can cause eruptive xanthomas" -> "Eruptive xanthomas may develop" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has a family history of myocardial infarction" -> "Possible metabolic syndrome" -> "Fenofibrate is used for dyslipidemia" -> "Dyslipidemia can lead to xanthomas" -> "Eruptive xanthomas may be present" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Elevated serum amylase indicates pancreatitis" -> "Pancreatitis can be associated with hyperlipidemia" -> "Fenofibrate is used to manage hyperlipidemia" -> "Hyperlipidemia can lead to eruptive xanthomas" -> "Eruptive xanthomas may be observed" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has abdominal pain and vomiting" -> "Physical exam shows tenderness in epigastrium" -> "Decreased bowel sounds suggest possible ileus" -> "Serum amylase elevation indicates pancreatitis" -> "Fenofibrate treatment initiated" -> "Eruptive xanthomas may develop due to lipid changes" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation suggests hyperlipidemia, likely due to familial hyperlipidemia, given the family history of early myocardial infarction and the elevated serum amylase. The initiation of therapy with fenofibrate indicates an attempt to manage this hyperlipidemia. Eruptive xanthomas are associated with severe hypertriglyceridemia, which can occur in familial hyperlipidemia. Therefore, further evaluation is most likely to show eruptive xanthomas.
